key_insight: Adaptive batch allocation in multi-objective Bayesian optimization can better balance information gain and optimization progress than fixed exploration policies in autonomous materials discovery.
engineering_relevance: For self-driving laboratories, this suggests campaign resources can be re-allocated on the fly to preserve Pareto-front discovery under budget, timeline, or experimental disruptions.
method: Benchmarked batch multi-objective BO for two alloy-design cases: a septenary RHEA and an Fe-Co-Ni soft magnetic alloy.
Compared exploitation-focused, fixed mixed, and two LLM-based adaptive resource-allocation strategies.
Evaluated responses under baseline conditions and mid-campaign disruptions such as budget cuts, timeline cuts, and combined constraints.
evidence_signal: Across the abstract’s evaluations, mixed allocation strategies gained substantially more mutual information than the exploitation-only baseline, and adaptive strategies outperformed fixed-mixed allocation under resource-event conditions.
watch_item: LLM-guided allocation may be sensitive to campaign-state estimation and resource-event interpretation, so robustness and reproducibility should be validated before deployment.
paper_title: Agentic Resource Allocation for Batch Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization in Autonomous Materials Discovery
